answer: Distributed ORAM hides access patterns while a group jointly serves a database, and the velvet of the construction is that the physical location of a record is independent of the logical query. The jetty of the design is that servers shuffle the data together without any one learning the permutation, so an observer cannot tell which identity was checked. A Sybil attacker watching the servers learns nothing about honest users, and the zephyr of the shuffling keeps the access pattern uniform.
